``` ::: ::: ## Test policy bar chart ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig <- plot_ly( df_counts, x = ~Policy_2026, y = ~pct/100, type = 'bar', marker = list( color = ifelse(df_counts$Policy_2026 == "Test Optional", sat_blue, sat_grey) ), text = ~paste0(round(pct, 1), "%"), # Text labels as percentages textposition = 'outside', # Place text above bars textfont = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial") # Match scatterplot style ) |> layout( title = list( text = "Test Policies in Sampled Schools for Fall 2026", x = 0.5, font = list(size = 18, color = "black", family = "Arial") # Match scatterplot title style ), xaxis = list( title = list(text="Admission Testing Requirement", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial") ), yaxis = list( title = list(text="Percent of Sampled Schools", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), tickformat = ".0%", range = c(0, 1) ), margin = list(t = 90) # Extra top margin for title ) |> config( staticPlot = TRUE ) fig ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Test tester When SAT scores are standardized, a one–standard deviation increase in a school’s average SAT score is associated with an approximately 15 percentage-point increase in six-year completion rates (p < 0.001). One standard deviation is about 150 SAT score points. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} value <- 0.15 ggplot() + annotate("text", x=0, y=0.7, label = paste0("Colleges have"), size = 6, hjust=0.5) + annotate("text", x=0, y=0.5, label = scales::percent(value), size = 20, fontface = "bold", color = sat_blue) + annotate("text", x=0, y=0.3, label = paste0("higher 6-year completion rates"), size = 6, hjust=0.5) + annotate("text", x=0, y=0.2, label = paste0("per 150 average SAT points above 1170"), size = 5, color="grey50") + theme_void() + xlim(-0.8, 0.8) + ylim(0, 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](testing_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Test taker line chart ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} year <- c(2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024) test_takers <- c(1637589, 1715481, 2136539, 2220087, 2198460, 1509133, 1737678, 1913742, 1973891) test_takers_df <- data.frame(year, test_takers) fig <- plot_ly( test_takers_df, x = ~year, y = ~test_takers/1e6, type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines+markers', line = list(color = sat_blue, width = 2), text = ~paste( "Year: ", year, "
Number of Students:", format(test_takers, big.mark = ",") ), hoverinfo = 'text' ) |> layout( title = list( text = "SAT Test Takers by Year (2016-2024)", x = 0.5, font = list(size = 16, color = "black", family = "Arial") ), xaxis = list( title = list(text="Year", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), fixedrange = TRUE ), yaxis = list( title = list(text="Number of Test Takers (millions)", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), tickformat = ".1f", fixedrange = TRUE ) ) |> config( modeBarButtonsToRemove = c( "select2d", # box select "lasso2d", # lasso select "toggleSpikelines" # optional extra buttons you might not want ), displaylogo = FALSE # removes Plotly logo ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Average Cost of Attendance: $", format(COSTT4_A, big.mark = ",") ), hoverinfo = 'text' ) |> layout( title = list( text = "Relationship Between Average SAT Scores and Average Cost of Attendance", font = list(size = 18, color = "black", family = "Arial"), x = 0.5 # centers the title like hjust = 0.5 ), margin = list(t = 90), xaxis = list( title = list(text = "SAT Average Score for Accepted Students", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), fixedrange = TRUE ), yaxis = list( title = list(text = "Cost of Attendance ($)", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), fixedrange = TRUE ), legend = list( title = list(text = "", font = list(size = 14, color = "black")), font = list(size = 12, color = "black") ), dragmode = "zoom" ) |> config( modeBarButtonsToRemove = c( "select2d", # box select "lasso2d", # lasso select "toggleSpikelines" # optional extra buttons you might not want ), displaylogo = FALSE # removes Plotly logo ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Cost and completion scatterplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig <- plot_ly(admin_df, x = ~C150_4, y = ~COSTT4_A, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers', marker = list(color = sat_blue), name = 'Schools', text = ~paste( "School: ", INSTNM, "

Completion Rate: ", scales::percent(C150_4, accuracy = 1) ), hoverinfo = 'text' ) |> layout( title = list( text = "Relationship Between School Cost of Attendance and Completion Rate", font = list(size = 18, color = "black", family = "Arial"), x = 0.5 # centers the title like hjust = 0.5 ), margin = list(t = 90), xaxis = list( title = list(text = "Undergraduate 6-Year Completion Rate", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), tickformat = ".0%", fixedrange = TRUE ), yaxis = list( title = list(text = "Cost of Attendance ($)", font = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), tickfont = list(size = 12, color = "black", family = "Arial"), fixedrange = TRUE ), legend = list( title = list(text = "", font = list(size = 14, color = "black")), font = list(size = 12, color = "black") ), dragmode = "zoom" ) |> config( modeBarButtonsToRemove = c( "select2d", # box select "lasso2d", # lasso select "toggleSpikelines" # optional extra buttons you might not want ), displaylogo = FALSE # removes Plotly logo ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Sat and admissions rates scatterplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} quad_fit <- lm(ADM_RATE ~ SAT_AVG + I(SAT_AVG^2), data = admin_df) #generating predicitons x_seq <- seq(min(admin_df$SAT_AVG, na.rm = TRUE), max(admin_df$SAT_AVG, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 200) pred_df <- data.frame(SAT_AVG = x_seq) pred <- predict(quad_fit, newdata = pred_df, interval = "confidence", level = 0.95) pred_df$fit <- pred[, "fit"] pred_df$lwr <- pred[, "lwr"] pred_df$upr <- pred[, "upr"] #chart fig <- plot_ly() |> # Scatter points add_trace(data = admin_df, x = ~SAT_AVG, y = ~ADM_RATE, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers', marker = list(color = sat_blue), name = 'Schools', text = ~paste( "School: ", INSTNM, "
Average SAT: ", SAT_AVG, "
Admission Rate: ", scales::percent(ADM_RATE, accuracy = 1) ), hoverinfo = 'text' ) |> # Regression line add_trace(data = pred_df, x = ~SAT_AVG, y = ~fit, type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines', line = list(color = sat_grey, width = 2), name = 'Line of Best Fit') |> # Confidence ribbon add_ribbons(data = pred_df, x = ~SAT_AVG, ymin = ~lwr, ymax = ~upr, fillcolor = 'rgba(70,130,180,0.2)', # semi-transparent steelblue line = list(color = 'transparent'), name = '95% CI') |> layout(title = list(text="Relationship Between SAT Average Scores and Admission Rates",tickfont = list(size = 16, color = "black", family = "Arial")), xaxis = list(title = "SAT Average Score for Accepted Students", fixedrange = TRUE, tickfont = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), yaxis = list(title = "Admission Rate", fixedrange = TRUE, tickformat = ".0%", tickfont = list(size = 14, color = "black", family = "Arial")), dragmode = "zoom") |> config( modeBarButtonsToRemove = c( "select2d", # box select "lasso2d", # lasso select "toggleSpikelines" # optional extra buttons you might not want ), displaylogo = FALSE # removes Plotly logo ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fig ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
